Council Minutes  7  02/02/2026
   Councilmember Madison noted his absence at the November 17,
  2025 meeting due to inclement weather that affected his work travel
  back to Pasadena and his ability to participate in this decision, and
  requested that the matter of Safe Parking at All Saints Church return
  to the full City Council.

  Mayor Gordo inquired regarding the legal effect of a deemed denial
  of the CEQA exemption. Caroline Monroy, Assistant City Attorney,
  stated that under the municipal code, if the City Council fails to act
  on a CEQA action, a failure to affirmatively approve or certify a
  CEQA action shall be deemed a denial thereof, and that a failure to
  act and any action taken pursuant to CEQA shall be considered a
  decision that may be called for review or appealed. She added that
  for the purpose of a quasi-judicial process, the failure to take action
  on CEQA is considered a decision under the City's municipal code.

  City Attorney Bagneris clarified that the item before the City Council
  at the moment would only be whether to approve a motion to rescind
  the closure of the public hearing and the deemed denial of CEQA,
  and to reopen and set a continued public hearing for a future City
  Council meeting. It should not be a discussion or decision on the
  merits of MCUP No. 7318 related to the All Saints Church application
  to establish a safe parking program.

  Mayor Gordo reported that he has spoken with tenants of The
  Maryland, congregants, and representatives from All Saints Church
  regarding this matter. Councilmember Jones added that Mayor
  Gordo and himself also met with the residents of the central district
  during his weekly neighborhood meeting and briefly discussed
  neighborhood issues, traffic, and crime in the area.

  Strefan Fauble, The Maryland HOA, spoke in opposition to the
  proposed action, and provided comments regarding an
  encounter between an unhoused individual and a bystander.

  Councilmember Hampton expressed concerns regarding potential
  legal implications from the matter and noted that he would "Abstain"
  when voting. He also noted that if the matter does move forward, he
  would then participate in the discussion, and consider the issue
  without bias as required in a quasi-judicial proceeding.

  Mayor Gordo expressed concerns that bringing the matter back to
  the City Council could create a slippery slope with future legal
  implications. He emphasized the importance of adhering to the City
  Council's procedure, the provisions contained in the Pasadena
  Municipal Code, and the process for conducting City business.

  Discussion ensued regarding the interpretation of the Pasadena
  Municipal Code, a deemed denied decision, and identifying a date
  for a proposed reopening and continuation of the public hearing.
